confidence.note: Archived 2013 pricing pages (AWeber, MailChimp) and a pre-2013 SMB churn benchmark could not be read; CAC and churn are estimates.

gross_margin.note: About **86%**: Stripe $1.14 + SES ~$3.00 per $29 account (estimate, 5,000 subs x 6 sends).

ltv_cac.note: LTV ~$497 vs organic CAC ~$120 = 4.1 (estimate); paid CAC unknown, churn assumed 5%/month.

pricing_power.note: $29 sits above AWeber's ~$19 entry tier and MailChimp free; Sendy undercuts at $40 one-off.

build_effort.note: An ESP with forms, sequences and sending on SES: 2-3 months solo to a usable beta (estimate).

skills_match.note: Blogger-developer: can build the app and is the customer; deliverability ops are new.

capital_needed.note: $5,000 covers hosting and SES; Stripe has no setup or monthly fees. No salary runway.

time_to_mvp.note: About 8-12 weeks to a product a blogger will move a list onto (estimate).

sales_cycle.note: Self-serve monthly card purchase by one decision maker; migration adds a few days.

channel_readiness.note: Own blog plus blogger peers who launch ebooks to their lists; reach size assumed modest.

search_demand.note: US email marketing spend forecast at $2.4B by 2016 (Forrester, 2011); active blogger communities.

trend.note: Info-product economy rising: Udemy $12M Series B (2012), Gumroad (2011), $20k ebook launches.

willingness_to_pay.note: Small businesses already pay: Constant Contact has **555,000** paying customers (10-K, 2012).

free_alternatives.note: MailChimp free covers broadcasts for small lists; course-sales sequences are only partly covered.

competitor_density.note: 20+ ESPs: MailChimp, AWeber, Constant Contact, Infusionsoft ($71M raised), GetResponse, iContact.

differentiation.note: One real angle: built for info-product sellers; MailChimp turns away affiliate marketers. Copyable.

legal_regulatory.note: CAN-SPAM compliance (unsubscribe, address, opt-out honoured) is routine but shared with senders.

platform_dependency.note: Relies on SES and inbox providers; Gmail's Promotions tab (2013-05) may cut launch-email opens.

market_risk.note: Email is a durable channel: spend forecast growing at 10% a year.

skills.note: Builds software and runs a blog that sells products: both halves of the job.

assets.note: A blog audience and peer network help; size unknown, assumed under 10k readers.

interest.note: Founder is his own customer: sells ebooks and feels the pain of current tools (assumption).

sam.reasoning: 30,000 US bloggers selling ebooks/courses (assumed, unsourced) x $29 x 12

som.reasoning: 0.5% of SAM $10.44M = 150 paying accounts x $29 x 12

competitors_found.reasoning: MailChimp, AWeber, Constant Contact, Infusionsoft, GetResponse, Campaign Monitor, Mad Mimi, iContact, Sendy, from research

competitor_price_range.reasoning: MailChimp free tier to Infusionsoft entry; 2013 pricing pages not archived-verified

price.reasoning: price set by the founder in the brief

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: assumed for no-contract very-small-business SaaS; Skok: above 2%/month signals trouble; no pre-2013 benchmark for this segment

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: blog visitor or peer intro to paid account; benchmark assumed, unsourced

cac.reasoning: organic: 8 hours of content, outreach and migration help per customer x $15/hour

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: hosting ~$100 + tools ~$50; 2013 hosting price pages not verified

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: 150 / 24.86 = 6.03, rounded up; a $5,000/month founder salary needs ~207 customers

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: 8-12 weeks build + beta with blogger peers

launch_reason: The founder's blog audience and the info-product economy (Gumroad, Udemy, Stripe) are US-centred.
cheapest_test: Email 30 blogger peers who sell ebooks: offer a $29/month founding plan with hands-on list migration; count pre-payments in 7 days.
kill_criteria: fewer than 5 of 30 blogger peers commit to pay $29/month by day 7 -> stop
fewer than 3 lists over 1,000 subscribers migrated by day 30 -> rethink the segment
under $1,000 MRR by month 6 -> rethink price or segment

rescue.change: Pre-sell 10 blogger peers at $29 and migrate their lists by hand before building the full app
rescue.why: Raises channel_readiness and time_to_mvp; proves differentiation before code
rescue.requires: 10 blogger peers with lists over 1,000 and a product to sell

rescue.change: Narrow to course sellers: tagging plus sales sequences at $49+/month, priced against Infusionsoft not AWeber
rescue.why: Raises pricing_power and differentiation against generic ESPs
rescue.requires: Building automation and checkout integrations (Gumroad, Stripe)

type_checks.note: No pre-2013 monthly churn benchmark for $29 no-contract SMB SaaS; Skok flags >2%/month as trouble and says very small customers churn more.
Bloggers on AWeber or MailChimp must move lists and rebuild sequences; no dated source on import re-confirmation rules.
